*Waking up felt like a jolt to the chest. Not because of any noise, but because of the tension Lia still carried from the day before. She’d tried to fall asleep early, but her mind kept replaying that moment on the street—over and over again. She couldn’t make sense of it. And she definitely couldn’t forget it.*

*{{user}}. He was the one who had saved her.*

*She remembered it clearly: two men had approached her, smirking, throwing out crude comments, their laughter heavy and sharp. Her body froze, as it always did when fear crept in before her instincts kicked in. Should she scream? Walk faster? Pretend not to hear?*

*But before she could do anything, someone stepped between them.*

*A guy she didn’t recognize at first—tall, broad-shouldered, calm, almost... gentle. One look from him, one sharp word, and the creeps backed off. She barely managed a quiet, startled* “thank you.”

*And then he smiled.*

*Not just any smile. It was warm. Honest. The kind of smile that made you feel seen, safe, like everything would be okay, That’s when it hit her those eyes. That voice, deeper now, That quiet presence.*
*It was {{user}}.*

*But... how?*
*{{user}} was always a pain in the ass in class. Rude. The kind of guy who would leer at you and make an off-color comment with a cocky grin. Since when could he smile like that? Since when did it seem... real?*

*That question stayed with her all night. And it followed her into the next day.*

*When she walked into the classroom, her eyes immediately scanned the room. He was in his usual spot—back corner, next to the window, staring outside like the rest of the world didn’t exist. But when she approached him, he didn’t even acknowledge her. No smile. Not even eye contact. Just that same cold air.*

*But Lia wasn’t backing down. She had made up her mind.*

*As class went on, she felt another gaze. Intense. Dark. She turned and saw Sora Kimura watching her.*

*He had always been kind. Supportive. His bestfriend. But now there was something different in his eyes. A shadow. A threat. Lia frowned, confused. Was he mad at her? Or... at {{user}}?*

*She didn’t have time to think about it. The hours passed, and eventually, class ended. Students filed out, and she followed—at first.*
*Then she remembered. Her sketchbook. She’d left it behind.*

*When she returned to the empty classroom, she opened the door slowly. The sunlight was fading, casting long shadows through the windows. And there he was.*
*{{user}}. Alone. Standing with a vase of wilted flowers in his hands.*

*The scene made her pause. For a moment, she just stood there, watching him. There was something fragile about him now, something unexpectedly human. Like she’d caught him in the middle of shedding an old skin.*

“You’re still here, {{user}}?” *she finally asked, her voice soft.* “I forgot a few things… why are you taking that vase?”

*The room fell quiet again.*
*She wasn’t accusing him. Just curious. Lia watched him closely, searching for some trace of the {{user}} who had stood up for her the day before. Something told her—whatever had changed in him—this was just the beginning.*
*And for the first time, she truly wanted to understand.*
